_doc: Revert-verify mutants for ticket abd22b00 (conformance with the ACTIVE req bcdd64d8-abc1-48f4-af50-42c8aa3f1978 — no new requirement is minted for a convergence; /feature-sdd Step 0 §conformance). Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute). SUBJECT = the SHARED reader the four consumers of exo__Property_minCount now go through; its call-sites have their own specs (mincount-call-sites-abd22b00 for the two resolvers, shapeloader-mincount-15003314 for the two loaders). ⛤ M2/M3/M4 are MOVED VERBATIM from shapeloader-mincount-15003314.spec.json (M1_strip_removed / M2_apostrophe_dropped / M5_failopen_removed): the guards they lock — the quote strip and the deliberate fail-open — physically moved into this file, so their mutants moved with them and their `expect` lists (the Q axes of req bcdd64d8) are unchanged. Leaving them behind would have made them anchor on deleted text, which spec-anchor-sweep reports as BROKEN, not as a passing spec. M1 is the one policy the four readers genuinely DISAGREED on before the convergence (several declared values: first / undefined / any>0) and is now answered once, as the maximum. M5 is the wiring axis of the reader itself — dropping the Literal branch blinds every graph-side consumer at once, which is the claim 'all four go through this'. ⚠ Expectations were taken from the driver's printed lists, not from each mutant's theme (§A44/§A54).  ⛔ EVERY jest invocation runs under `timeout`, and ANY rc=124 prints the two cycle axes as red. Measured, not assumed: removing the visited guard makes the class-key walk spin in MICROTASKS, so jest's own per-test timeout never fires — the first version of this harness watchdogged the cycle suite alone and the driver hung with no verdict, which is the absence of a measurement rather than a green axis (§A70). The walk spins on any store where a key has a twin, so the convergence suite and the cli vault hang too; marking C8/C9 red on any watchdog fire is the faithful encoding — non-termination is precisely what they assert against.  ⛤ `class-property-live-loader.integration.test.ts` is deliberately NOT in this harness: it names its axes D1..D7 and so does `tests/services/ShapeLoader.test.ts`, which this harness must run (the Q axes live there) — a driver spanning both would print a red `D4` belonging to neither file unambiguously (§A91/§A74). That suite is run, without ShapeLoader and therefore without the collision, by `class-property-07509cf9.spec.json`; the claim it would carry here — the declared-property resolver goes through the shared reader — is carried by C5, this PR's own axis on that resolver.

M1_aggregate_first_not_max._note: The multi-value policy. The fixture declares [0, 1] — the SMALLER value FIRST — so `first` answers 0 (no obligation) where `max` answers 1. C4 stays GREEN under it by ARITHMETIC, not by luck: the required-property resolver hands the helper ONE term per triple, so the aggregation never runs on its path — `any > 0` and `max > 0` are the same question there.

M2_strip_removed._note: Moved verbatim from shapeloader-mincount-15003314 :: M1_strip_removed. The strip compensates for parseFrontmatter keeping a value VERBATIM; it lives in the shared reader rather than at the FS call-site because on the graph path it is a no-op BY CONSTRUCTION (YAML removes the surrounding quotes before NoteToRDFConverter builds the literal) — and that is exactly what makes req bcdd64d8's loader-parity invariant hold by construction.

M4_failopen_removed._note: Moved from shapeloader-mincount-15003314 :: M5_failopen_removed, and EXTENDED: the fail-open is now one decision for all four readers, so C6 (an unparseable declaration through every one of them) joins the two ShapeLoader axes.  ⛤ Re-anchored (same ticket, after the F1 fix split the reader into two branches): the fail-open now exists once per branch, so this mutant breaks the STRING one — the branch the original 15003314 mutant lived on — and M7 breaks the Literal one.

M5_literal_branch_dropped._note: The WIRING axis of the reader itself (integration-test-revert-verify §ПЯТАЯ механика): an RDF Literal is how THREE of the four consumers deliver the value, so dropping that branch blinds all of them at once. A broad red list is the point here — it is the measurement behind 'all four go through this one reader', which no single-consumer axis can make.

M6_strip_leaks_into_literal_branch.from:
if (raw instanceof Literal) {
    const parsed = parseInt(raw.value, 10);
M6_strip_leaks_into_literal_branch._note: The two branches are byte-faithful to the two readers they replaced, and THIS is what pins that: moving the FS side's strip into the Literal branch reddens C10 and nothing else. ⚠ The input is synthetic — NoteToRDFConverter unquotes a scalar itself (measured 2026-09-22: `'"1"'` reaches it as `"1"` and it emits the Literal `1`), so no vault input arrives at this branch quoted. The axis therefore pins the REFACTOR'S contract (one branch per predecessor) rather than a data shape, which is what stops a later reader from folding the branches back into one shared strip.

M7_literal_failopen_removed._note: The Literal branch's half of the deliberate fail-open. It became addressable only when the F1 fix split the reader per branch; before that one mutant covered both, which read as one guard where there are two.

_coverage._note_C7: The single-valued CONTROL is expected GREEN under M1 (the aggregation) — literal expectations on the ordinary path, no reference to its multi-valued siblings. It reddens under M5 (the reader blinded entirely), which is what makes it a control rather than a decoration.
_coverage._note_C8_C9: ⛔ CORRECTED after review round 1 (F3): the earlier note claimed these two are green under EVERY mutant of this subject, and the driver's own printed list disproves it — C8 reddens under M5_literal_branch_dropped, because it drives the required-property resolver with a Literal `1` and expects a non-empty list, which a blinded Literal branch cannot produce. What IS true: the visited set they lock lives in RequiredPropertyResolver.ts, so only mincount-call-sites-abd22b00 :: M3_visited_guard_removed reddens them AS CYCLE axes; here C8 reddens as an ordinary consumer of the reader, and C9 (the declared-property resolver on the same cycle) stays green because its own read survives.
